answer: A grove of agents can require each new identity to post a refundable stake before it may influence a shared decision. Votes are weighted by stake, while a challenge period lets peers flag linked accounts; proven duplicates forfeit their deposits, which are redistributed to honest participants. This does not make Sybils impossible, but forces an attacker to lock up capital for every identity and risk losing it. A long voyage of repeated challenges raises that cost, while a terrace of independent reviewers helps prevent one clique from falsely accusing rivals.
